overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a December 5 meeting at City Hall without an ADA-compliant access point, but found no violation from broadcast audio glitches; only compliance was ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the December 5 in-person meeting was held at City Hall, where the only access point was not accessible to people with disabilities.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a meeting at a location that, at the time, lacked ADA compliant access to the meeting location.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged audio glitches during the broadcast of the December 5 meeting made part of the meeting inaudible.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find that the audio disruptions in the meeting broadcast violated the Open Meeting Law in this instance where the meeting was held in-person and individuals in attendance at the meeting were able to see and hear the discussions.

remedy: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Council that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
